No agenda statement (what the call will cover, how long it takes) and no explicit 'sound good?' before diving into discovery.
Never asked about stairs/floors at origin or destination.
Never asked about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony).
Never asked about special access considerations (narrow hallways, tight turns, long walks).
Never asked how many boxes the customer estimated needing.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.
Never asked about access concerns (elevator, parking, HOA restrictions).
Never asked a moving-stressors question — missed an easy opening given the customer volunteered he broke his leg.
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener before quoting rates.
Didn't list what's included in the hourly rate (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools).

No mention of Meet Your Mover email.

Clock mechanics never explained — no mention that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips and no 'take a carload' tip, despite a customer who is physically limited (broken leg) and would benefit most from pre-move prep advice.
Never made an explicit close attempt to lock in a date on the call ('want to go ahead and get that booked?') — left it as 'just let us know.'
Never stated that no deposit is required.
No email handoff at all — no confirmation email mentioned, no bolded key-details list, no 'reply with any corrections' step.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'

Gave inconsistent pricing figures during the call (full-service quote wobbled between ~$3,600, ~$5,000, and move-only between $1,900–$2,500 and $2,200), which could leave the customer unsure of the real number — relevant to Einstein's estimate-accuracy focus.
No insurance explanation (No Worries coverage + 60¢/lb baseline never mentioned).
No rapport-building or humor moment — call stayed transactional throughout.
top_strength: When the customer balked at the ~$5,000 full pack-and-move estimate, Joel pivoted immediately and clearly to the lower-cost option (customer packs, Einstein just moves, ~$1,900-2,500) — solid budget-conscious framing that kept a price-sensitive lead engaged instead of losing him to sticker shock.
coaching_note: Joel (listed as Operations Manager, likely covering phones rather than a trained sales rep) never learned or used the customer's name, skipped agenda-setting, the Save Your Ass prep speech, and the entire email/booking close — the call ends with no date locked, no deposit-free mention, and no confirmation email, so a warm, price-sensitive lead is walking away with nothing but a verbal range of numbers that shifted twice during the call. If ops staff are regularly picking up sales calls, this one is a good case for a quick refresher on the core close: get the name, use it, and always follow the quote with a same-call email handoff.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine empathy on 'Oh, sorry to hear that' about the broken leg and a natural, unscripted pivot to a cheaper option, but otherwise transactional with visible fumbling over the numbers and no name use to build rapport.
audio_review_reason: Transcript shows noticeable garbling and false starts around the pricing numbers ('We Typic.', 'we're an $1,800') alongside inconsistent restated totals ($3,600/$5,000 vs. $1,900-2,500/$2,200) — worth an audio check to confirm whether the confusion is a transcription artifact or the rep actually gave the customer conflicting numbers live.
